The origins of the modern telecommunications satellite date to Sputnik, the first orbital man-made satellite, launched by the former Soviet Union in 1957. The first fully functional telecommunications satellite was Earlybird I launched by the United States in 1965...

Satellites have provided the ability to communicate with voice, video, and data around the globe. Advanced technology applications such as DBS (Direct Broadcast Satellite) TV and GPS (Global Positioning System) would have been impossible without the development of satellite radio technology...

Telecommunications satellites are microwave relay devices located far above the earth, and therefore, far above the horizon. The satellite's "view" of the earth is a direct line-of-sight path and may be expanded or collapsed depending on altitude. Theoretically, three satellites could cover the entire earth, with the exception of the Polar Regions.....
Satellite communications systems compete, and cooperate, with earth based (terrestrial) technologies such as microwave, fiber optics, cable, and ground based radio.

Traditional satellite telecommunications systems use Geosynchronous Earth Orbiting (GEO) space vehicles. Geosynchronous means the satellite is stationary if viewed from the earth's surface, or completes an orbit every 24 hours.
DISCUSSION

GEOs orbit at an altitude of 22,237 miles (36,0000 km) and support Fixed Satellite System (FSS) requirements. The Space Shuttle orbits much lower and is in an asynchronous orbit (completing a complete orbit every 90 minutes)...
Space Shuttle: 1 rotation every 90 minutes......

GEOs have a large "Footprint" (area of coverage on the earth). Frequencies range from 130 MHz to 30 GHz and each of the satellites is positioned approximately 2 degrees apart to prevent interference. Currently, there are at least 192 GEOs in service...

Satellite communications links consist of an uplink (RF transmitted from an earth terminal) and downlink (RF transmitted by a space vehicle). The links spend most of their airtime in the vacuum of space, where attenuation is not an issue. This advantage is lost when the links propagate through the earth's atmosphere. The links utilize a frequency separation scheme to prevent interference and help defeat the bending effects that the atmosphere has on high frequency RF. The downlink is always a lower frequency than the uplink...

In order to maximize the strength of the uplink, the transmitted beam is highly focused. The transmit element is centered in a concave, reflective dish antenna.

The downlink is focused on a particular footprint. When regional concerns require higher resolution, a spot beam antenna may be used to focus the beam into a small area of coverage within the footprint...
The satellite broadcast can support a huge number of ground stations within the footprint. This makes an FSS ideal for point-to-multipoint communications networks-one uplink and multiple downlinks...

All satellite radio systems are divided into 2 parts - Earth Segment and Space Segment. Both segments have the same basic components; antennae, reflective dishes, and supporting electronics. e size of the dish relates directly to the frequency range of the system. As an example, Intelsat I (launched in 1968) had dishes measuring 90 feet in diameter. Direct Broadcast Satellite (DBS) antennas are 12 inches in diameter.....

Very Small Aperture Terminals (VSATs) are the latest type of earth segment systems operating in C and Ka-bands. VSAT is deployed to support private point-to-multipoint networks. Applications include banking, credit verification, and inventory management...
VSAT bandwidth is in the 2.4 Kbps - 20 Mbps range. Generally, 64 Kbps data rate service is provided with an aggregate of
512 Kbps for the entire network. Nearly 1,000,000 VSAT terminals are installed worldwide. A large VSAT network could have up to 5,000 terminals.

Satellite systems can support a number of transponders and therefore have a substantial amount of aggregate bandwidth. A single transponder may provide up to 36 MHz of bandwidth. As a point of reference, Intelsat I could support 240 voice channels. Intelsat VI can support 120,000 voice and 3 TV channels...
Satellite links are susceptible to environmental interference, particularly in frequencies above 20 GHz (Ka-band). Lower frequencies may compete directly with terrestrial microwave
(C band). Satellite systems require extensive error detection, self-test, and automatic correction capabilities.

GEOs were designed to operate at extremely long range (over 22,000 miles). Although area of coverage and number of terminals makes a satellite system look like the best radio solution, propagation delay and response time are certainly major detractors...

It takes at least 250 milliseconds for RF energy to make the round trip between the earth and space segments. Considering on board processing time, the delay can easily be extended to more than 600 milliseconds (over 1/2 second). Interactive voice, video, and data are not delay tolerant...

Satellites are commonly used for video teleconferencing. How can this be done if there are delays in the transmission? The satellite broadcast is in lecture mode only. brid mode of operation may be used too, such as watching the lecturer on a TV screen, but responding via a landline voice circuit. Internet access is also being offered, on a limited basis, using a similar hybrid approach.....

A hybrid mode of operation may be used too, such as watching the lecturer on a TV screen, but responding via a landline voice circuit. Internet access is also being offered, on a limited basis, using a similar hybrid approach...

National, regional and local regulatory bodies control satellite system segments. Health and safety regulations may impact the placement of terrestrial segment equipment. Frequency allocation is necessary to prevent interference and organize telecommunications assets...

Low-Earth Orbiting (LEO) and Middle-Earth Orbiting (MEO) satellites operate at much lower altitudes than the GEOs and support Mobile Satellite System (MSS) technologies. LEOs operate from 644 to 2,415 miles and MEOs from 10,062 to 20,940 miles...

Unlike FSS space vehicles, which are placed in equatorial orbit slots, MSS space vehicles are positioned in groups called "Constellations". For example, the Iridium Constellation designed by Motorola has 66 space vehicles. 11 satellites, plus
1 spare, are placed in 6 orbital planes at an altitude of 421.5 miles.

Iridium represents the premier deployment of MSS, but not without problems. The owners defaulted on their loans and the creditors took over in 1999. Regardless of its shortfalls, Iridium will be used as an example of a high-technology satellite communications system.

The Iridium concept involved end users subscribing to a network with fantastic capabilities. All hardware and software were unique to Iridium. An Iridium phone could communicate with another Iridium phone, anywhere on the globe. The phone link was L-Band (1.616-1.626 GHz) and inter-satellite links were Ka-Band (23.18023.38 GHz).....

Propagation delays with LEOs are minimal due to the relatively short range between segments. Additionally, the inter-satellite links are operating in the vacuum of space and do not suffer from attenuation. A LEO network is like a cellular phone network in reverse. The phones are fixed (relatively) and the cells are mobile.....
The cellular hand-off process is also performed in reverse; the space segment has to hand-off the user as the cells move overhead. If a call were placed to a non-subscriber, up to
12 regional gateways would be utilized to switch the call to a conventional telephone network.

Iridium was an incredible concept, both technologically and financially. The total capital investment was close to $5 billion and a Iridium phone would cost around $4000. idering the possibilities, the cost may have been worth it. Imagine a climber on the summit of Mount Everest talking to miner in Death Valley; both people are communicating simultaneously on portable hand-held telephones.....

Another form of LEO MSS network is the Teledesic network. The word is a combination of Tele, meaning distance, and geodesic, meaning the shortest distance between two points on a given surface. The concept involves the deployment of up to 288 LEOs...

Teledesic satellites would operate as low as 400 miles and therefore counteract many of the effects of atmospheric attenuation. The intent of the system is to provide Internet access via a satellite gateway. A relatively inexpensive two-way dish connected to the computer would afford the user World Wide Web connectivity.....

Satellite communications systems are usually deployed to support point-to-multipoint network topologies. The satellite is a single asset that must be shared by multiple users. User data must not be lost or traded, although delays are tolerable. Sharing the satellite in a cooperative manner is called multiple access.....

Technology provides several multiple access methods, each having strengths and weaknesses. Hybrid methods may be developed by combining circuitry and/or software. The following multiple access methods will be addressed: ...
Space or Location Frequency Division (FDMA)
Time and Frequency Demand Assignment (DAMA)

Space Division Multiple Access (SDMA) takes advantage of the space between the stations on the earth to achieve multiple access. Separate messages are directed to different earth stations on the same frequency. SDMA is made possible with multi-beam antennas or high-speed switches....

Frequency Division Multiple Access (FDMA) uses a frequency allocation plan to ensure each earth station has a unique RF frequency assigned. Essentially, FDMA is accomplished by dividing the satellites bandwidth. Intelsat satellites have been using FDMA for years with great success....

Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) is similar in concept to FDMA, except time slots are allocated instead of bandwidth. Each earth station accesses the satellite at the same frequency but must conform to a time sequence. TDMA transmissions are "bursty" because data is sent in time segments...

Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA), a Spread Spectrum technique, uses a code sequence to identify the message. The code must be synchronized between the satellite and the earth station. CDMA has excellent interference reduction capabilities and can accommodate a large number of users...

Random Multiple Access (RMA) has the ability to accommodate a very large number of users with private hot lines. Individual calls are connected simultaneously without retransmission delays or network synchronization. RMA uses Spread Spectrum technology and requires a baseband receiver circuit for each user station.....

The next element of the satellite system to be presented is electronic circuits. Space segment circuits must conform to stringent controls for weight, space available, and shielding. h station circuits tend to be higher performance than space segment equivalents. For example, a satellite power amplifier may generate up to 20 watts, while an earth station power amplifier may generate greater than 2 kilowatts.....

Earth station circuits tend to be higher performance than space segment equivalents. For example, a satellite power amplifier may generate up to 20 watts, while an earth station power amplifier may generate greater than 2 kilowatts.

Uplink transmission is accomplished at the earth station with Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) or Klystron amplifiers. Both types can generate kilowatt power levels. The output is then sent to the antenna...

Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) amplifiers are high gain, low noise, and wide bandwidth microwave electron tubes. Operating frequencies are from 300 MHz to 50 GHz. The TWT is primarily a voltage amplifier that can boost RF signals 40 dB...

Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) amplifiers are high gain, low noise, and wide bandwidth microwave electron tubes. Operating frequencies are from 300 MHz to 50 GHz. The TWT is primarily a voltage amplifier that can boost RF signals 40 dB.

dB - The decibel (dB), one tenth of a bel, is the logarithmic ratio between input and output. An increase of 3 dB indicates a doubling of the power; conversely, -3 dB is a halving of the power. The TWT output of 20 dB is 100 times the input. Some TWTs are capable of 40 dB or 10,000 times the input.
DEFINITION

Klystron tubes also serve as amplifiers for the uplink. Klystrons are tunable and operate in the same general range as TWTs but have less gain. Klystrons may also be used as oscillators in other electronics applications...
Since the antenna is used for both transmitting and receiving, something has to prevent the transmitter from blowing out the rather sensitive receiver. This is accomplished with a diplexer.

The diplexer isolates the transmitter from the receiver by using bandpass filters on the receiver input. Similar filters are used in the transmit path to ensure that received frequencies are directed to the receivers only..

Earth segment receivers need to be very sensitive and have special amplifiers to capture the weak satellite downlink from space. Low Noise Block Converters (LNBs) or Low Noise Amplifiers (LNAs) circuits are used. The LNB is physically located at the focal point of the parabolic satellite dish...
The LNA is typically supported by a Field-Effect Transistor (FET).

The down-converter changes the extremely high frequency satellite downlink into an intermediate frequency, usually in the C-Band, permitting the RF to be processed via coaxial cable.
